text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: sustained p99 decode latency spike on streaming endpoints (us-west-2). p95 ~3x baseline, p99 ~8x baseline. Spike started ~1739998800. Suspected cause: kernel/compilepath rollout (trt8 + flashattn + new compiler flags) rolled at 1739998600. Auto-fallbacks failing on some hosts. Alerting #eng-sre and oncall @tara_oncall.

tara_oncall: seeing it too, dashboards show streaming tail at ~1.9s p99 (normal ~180ms). Impacting streaming chat + realtime infer pipeline.

maria: confirmed customer reports for embedding ingestion delays. A few high-volume customers seeing errors/timeouts. Ticket count up.

kai: quick check — kernel build 774 (trt8-upgrade) went to canary -> prod at 1739998600. compile flags rolled: -march=znver4, -O3-sched, and a custom flashattn patch.

jon: any immediate mitigation? can we pin back to 773 or roll a rollback?

tara_oncall: trying to scope blast radius. Running `rg "compilepath" /var/logs/runtime -n | head` to map hosts.

maria: trace snippets show decode kernel paging spikes (pagefault-style stalls) followed by connection resets on stream clients. Example log: ```
[2026-03-15T02:18:12Z] decode_worker[pid=2234] WARN tail_decode: paging stall 512ms kernel=774
[2026-03-15T02:18:13Z] stream_conn[client=acme] ERROR reset write timeout
```

kai: looks like KV cache eviction + new kernel's memory allocator behavior under continuous-batching triggers heavy tail. I see increased minor page faults and TLB invalidation counts in perf counters.

jon: can we route streaming traffic away from affected pool? Is there a routing policy to prefer kernel 773 nodes?

tara_oncall: yes - using the smart routing controlplane. I'm initiating a soft-reroute to fallback-pool (kernel=773) for streaming-tagged routes. Command: `./bin/controlplane reroute --route streaming --from pool-prod-774 --to pool-prod-773 --gradual 30s`

release-bot: deploy event detected — rollback plan available. `deploy/rollforward-773` created by kai at 1739998900.

maria: reroute started, monitoring. Early signs: p95 improving on rerouted envs but still noisy for in-flight streams; p99 remains elevated because some long-lived streams are pinned.

kai: quick mitigation: disable the new flashattn microkernel patch on a subset of 774 nodes (hotpatch) and leave rest for telemetry. Patch command: `ssh node && pkill -USR1 runtime && echo disable_flashmicro=1 > /etc/runtime/flags` (doing on 4 hosts now).

jon: good. Also recommend temporary lowering batching window to reduce memory pressure: set `BATCH_MAX_MS=12` on the streaming service via config rollout. That reduces throughput but lowers tail risk.

tara_oncall: applying BATCH_MAX_MS change to canary first. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/streamer BATCH_MAX_MS=12 -n runtime-prod --record`

maria: customer impact update: Policy service (risk-scorer) p99 up ~2.2s, some timeouts causing retry storms. Notified CS leads, advising to throttle retries.

kai: perf counters confirm decrease in pagefaults on hotpatched hosts. Suggest we keep reroute + hotpatch + batch window for 30m while we observe.

jon: agree. Is there a known compiler flag in this rollout that could cause the allocator to favor huge pages or different mremap behavior?

kai: yes the rollout toggled `-fuse-ld=gold` and a custom allocator shim that alters madvise/hint patterns. Suspect interaction with FlashAttention's contiguous allocation strategy.

tara_oncall: at 1739998920 reroute shows 60% traffic on fallback pool; p95 on fallback ~220ms, p99 ~350ms. On original pool p99 still >1.6s.

maria: adding incident severity note: SLOs breached for streaming p99 in us-west-2. Customer impact: delayed inference for real-time features, some timed-out sessions. CS notified, high-touch customers contacted.

jon: next steps: 1) keep reroute in place until patch validated 2) roll hotpatch to all 774 nodes if metrics keep improving 3) revert allocator flag in a follow-up build if needed 4) prepare rollback to 773 image if no improvement in 45m.

kai: I'll assemble a minimal reproducible job to stress KV cache and allocate pattern so we can test a patch locally. Also opening a PR to revert the allocator shim (PR #4627).

tara_oncall: handing off to @jon for the next shift at 1739999005. Summary for next oncall: reroute active, hotpatch applied to subset (aim to finish), BATCH_MAX_MS=12 in canary then rollout, PR #4627 open to revert allocator shim, watch p99 and pagefault counters, customer tickets updated.

jon: taking over. I'll set an alert threshold to notify again if p99 > 800ms or pagefault count spikes >2x baseline. Also will coordinate with platform to schedule a rollback to 773 if we don't see steady improvement in 45m.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigating, assignee=jon, priority=high, incident_id=INC-2026-0315-42.

maria: leaving notes for postmortem: timeline of kernel rollout, compile flags, flashattn microkernel opt, observed pagefault/TLB metrics, reroute/hotpatch timings, customer impact and tickets.

jon: noted. I'll run a runbook with steps and owners and tag product + security for impact review.

release-bot: changelog snippet created: "Revert allocator shim if mitigations insufficient; track PR #4627".

tara_oncall: thanks team. I'll be reachable if anything spikes; otherwise jon will continue monitoring. :thumbsup:
